To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new approach was developed for the preparation of surfaces for IgG binding featuring reduced nonspecific adsorbance and antifouling properties, without the need of energy-intensive and/or environmentally aggressive surface pretreatment.
we have developed a method to prepare antifouling, low nonspecific adsorbing protein-based surfaces by combining the use of a protein-polymer bioconjugate with the in situ polymerization of PEGMA.

a new method for preparing antifiouling surfaces with low nonspecific binding is demonstrated, which does not require any energy-intensive or environmentally-aggressive surface pretreatment, and which can be applied to any hydrophobic substrate, including polypropylene.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and characterization of a new strategy for the preparation of antioleophobic and low nonspecific binding surfaces on hydrophobic substrata, without the need of energy-intensive pretreatments.

the preparation of protein–polymer bioconjugates for surfaces with antifouling features and low nonspecific binding, which are of particular interest for biomedical applications, such as implantable devices, biosensors, and tissue engineering.
the preparation of antithrombotic surfaces, which are able to resist the adhesion of blood platelets and thrombus formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of hydrophobin self-assembly with in situ Cu(0)-initiated polymerization of PEGA allows to prepare surfaces with antifouling properties and low nonspecific binding, and that the use of hydrophobically modified protein A as a model protein for surface functionalization allows to achieve a significant reduction of nonspecific adsorption.
the proposed approach is an efficient and versatile method for the preparation of protein-based surfaces with antifouling properties.
the presented method is a very promising strategy for the preparation of surfaces with low nonspecific binding, which is a key requirement in many biomedical applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the self-assembling protein-PPEGMA bioconjugates could be a promising strategy for the development of antifouled surfaces, with low nonspecific binding, for the use of protein A in affinity chromatography.
the combination of hydrophobin and PEGA is a promising approach to prepare surfaces with antifouling features and low nonspecific binding.

the use of a self-assembling protein to achieve the surface immobilization of the initiator for the polymerization of a polymer brush with antifouling properties is a promising approach to prepare surfaces with antifouing features on a variety of substrates, without requiring the use of pretreatment steps.
The main takeaway from our work is that

protein-based surfaces can be prepared on hydrophobic supports by using a simple self-assembly process followed by a controlled radical polymerisation, thus opening the way to a new class of surfaces with antifouling features and low nonspecific binding.

the use of self-assembling protein-polymer bioconjugates is an effective strategy to achieve surfaces with antifouling properties and low nonspecific binding, and that this approach is particularly suitable for poorly reactive hydrophobically modified surfaces.
the combination of hydrophobin and Cu(0)-living radical polymerization is a promising route to prepare antifouling, low nonspecific binding surfaces on poorly reactive substrates.
